direction.premise: A duel of royal laws turns privately chosen decree cards into public changes on a shared board.
direction.composition: The shared royal board is followed by the current laws and a hand of selectable illustrated decree cards.
direction.shapeLanguage: Printed card rectangles, board cells, royal insignia and the recovered ornamental drawings carry the tabletop identity.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Source card and board artwork is retained as printed surfaces with muted parchment, ink and metal accents.
direction.paletteLogic: Parchment grounds the hand while faction and effect colors distinguish the consequences of each decree.
direction.typography: Original card typography keeps decree names above their concise rule effects; room controls use compact system labels.
direction.signature: Each player seals a private decree; neither opponent hand nor future deck appears in the other client before the reveal.
direction.distinction: FOG uses geographic orders and ZAMAZKA uses painted restoration fragments; this port retains its source game object and the specific input loop described here.

architecture.primaryVerb: Select an illustrated decree from your own hand, seal it, then read the combined law and shared board consequence.
architecture.physicalFeedback: A selected card is marked immediately; after both choices the round advances and the new public state persists.
architecture.spatialRationale: The shared royal board is followed by the current laws and a hand of selectable illustrated decree cards. This keeps the current game object and its real inputs spatially connected on a phone.

production.renderer: The original DOM board, card renderer and local authored artwork make individual rules readable without canvas text scaling.
production.focalAsset: The retained decree illustrations and board provide the playable focal objects; the new crown-on-board SVG identifies the port.

motion.character: A selected card is marked immediately; after both choices the round advances and the new public state persists.
motion.action: Select an illustrated decree from your own hand, seal it, then read the combined law and shared board consequence.
motion.anticipation: The current selection, room state and available control labels expose the pending operation before the player activates it.
motion.response: The next visible state responds to the actual control: Each player seals a private decree; neither opponent hand nor future deck appears in the other client before the reveal.
motion.followThrough: The resulting world, board or round state remains visible until a later explicit action changes it; no decorative transition hides the outcome.
motion.interruption: Repeated input uses the current state; pointer cancellation releases held controls and hidden tabs stop transmitting held actions.
motion.reducedMotion: The complete play state remains legible without decorative entry animations; spatial gameplay and authoritative outcomes retain their original timing.

evidence.expectedChange: The network room controls open while the retained local AI and hotseat choices remain available.
